clue.text: Dog savaged Republicans and odd characters in melee

indicators.note: something savaged is torn apart, so these letters are mauled into a new order
the first, third and fifth letters of melee are taken

explanation.surface: A dog tears into a crowd of Republican politicians in a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters in' melee gives MLE, which joins REPUBLICANS in the pool that 'savaged' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clumber spaniel is a heavy English breed of gundog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Superhero playing a cinematic part endlessly, top class

indicators.note: playing about with letters, like a performer improvising, signals that they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the word's final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes
A is the conventional letter for first-rate or top class

explanation.surface: An actor takes on a film role as a superhero, perfectly cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PART to PAR; A + CINEMATIC + PAR is rearranged by 'playing', and A for top class closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain America is a Marvel comics hero, so he is an example of a superhero.

clue.text: Pretentious type bitter after good times

indicators.note: after puts the bitter piece following the good-times piece

parts.note: ups, as in ups and downs, are good times
tart means sharp or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: A social climber is resentful once the good days are over.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen who behaves with unearned self-importance, a pretentious type.

clue.text: Popular film? Ban one about train robber

parts.note: to block something is to ban or stop it
Buster is the 1988 film about Buster Edwards, one of the Great Train Robbers

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop a film being made about a notorious train robber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Train Robbery was a famous 1963 British mail-train heist; the film Buster told one robber's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster is a hugely successful film, the question mark noting that it is defined by its popularity.

clue.text: One's in group carrying out rebellion

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the group word

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang
one is I, and one's stands for I is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone belonging to a gang is busy carrying out an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying out' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt, a synonym for rebellion.

clue.text: Out-of-date teacher departed

parts.note: passé means no longer fashionable
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned schoolmaster has left the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed on is a euphemism for died, the same sense as departed.

clue.text: Nick's suspension overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue overturned means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a ban is a suspension, as from playing

explanation.surface: A footballer named Nick sees his suspension quashed on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick's' looks like a name; it is the verb to steal, with 's for is.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab and to nick are both slang for steal or arrest.

clue.text: Perfect example of Eastern book with religious content

parts.note: pi, short for pious, describes religious content
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: An Eastern scripture is held up as a model of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is the ideal embodiment of a type, a perfect example of it.

clue.text: Romantic laments tiniest failing

indicators.note: a failing structure collapses, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A poet mourns even the smallest shortcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimentalist indulges in tender, nostalgic feeling, which makes them a romantic.

clue.text: Ministers enact legislation carrying half of Conservatives

indicators.note: carrying means the outer word holds the other piece

parts.note: to pass a bill is to enact legislation

indicators.note: half of takes the first three letters of the six-letter word

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Government ministers pass laws with the backing of some Tory MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' suggests politicians, but here they are clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastors are Christian clergy, and ministers is another name for clergy.

clue.text: Superb vehicle overturned by tree

indicators.note: overturned means the vehicle word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
the lime or linden is a tree

explanation.surface: A vehicle flipped over beside a tree, which hardly sounds superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means of the highest excellence, so it is a synonym of superb.

clue.text: Captain Cook's equipment

definitions.meaning: a Turkish military commander or chief officer
a brand of heavy range cooker

explanation.surface: Kitchen gear belonging to the explorer Captain Cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captain Cook' reads as the explorer; split it into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an Ottoman commander, and a cast-iron kitchen range found in many British country homes.

clue.text: One doing more good deeds in beauty spot

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, a Scout who is kinder than the others
A moorland plateau and walking spot in the Peak District

explanation.surface: A Scout earns praise for doing extra good turns at a scenic place.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinder Scout is the highest point in England's Peak District National Park; Scouts are pledged to do a good deed daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peak District plateau is a celebrated beauty spot, and a more benevolent Scout is literally a kinder one.

clue.text: Scrapping briefly, risk rough Russian fighter holding part of leg

indicators.note: rough treatment roughs up the letters of risk into a new order
holding means the aircraft word contains the leg word

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
the shin is the front part of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A rough Russian fighter takes a knock to the leg in a brief scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns RISK into SKIR; MIG holding SHIN gives MISHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirmishing is engaging in short, minor fights, so it is fighting briefly.

clue.text: Still batting with no suggestion of criticism bagging duck

indicators.note: bagging means catching and holding, so the outer phrase takes the inner letter

parts.note: no tut is no disapproving click of the tongue
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shown as O

explanation.surface: A cricketer survives at the crease without criticism despite nearly making no score.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is not out is still in at the end of an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a batsman not dismissed, who is therefore still in and batting.

clue.text: Venue for performing music — ole!

indicators.note: performing music means playing it, so the letters are played around into a new order

explanation.surface: A hall where music is played to shouts of olé.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coliseum is a London opera house, and any coliseum is a large arena or venue.

clue.text: Shabby old Italian leader, a communist

parts.note: the doge was the elected ruler of Venice or Genoa
red is a common word for a communist

explanation.surface: A former Italian head of state turns out to be a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eared book has worn, folded page corners, so it looks shabby and well used.

clue.text: Change meat, put in starters of aloo and insalata

indicators.note: put, with in, says letters are placed into the meat word; here the second goes in after the T
in places the first starting letter inside the meat word, after its opening three letters

parts.note: mutton is the meat of sheep

indicators.note: starters, the opening courses, means the first letter of aloo is taken
of completes the phrase starters of, which applies to insalata too, taking its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook alters the meat dish, adding a potato curry and a salad as starters.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters go in separately: A after MUT and I after the second T. Aloo is potato in Indian cooking; insalata is Italian for salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutation is an alteration or change, especially in genetic material.

clue.text: Cart in which acrobat swaps sides

indicators.note: swaps sides means the letters for left and right change places

parts.note: a tumbler is an acrobat who does somersaults

explanation.surface: A circus acrobat changes position inside a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swaps sides' exchanges L (left) and R (right), changing LER to REL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel is a farm cart that tips, famous for taking victims to the guillotine.

clue.text: Girl — I turn with repulsion, embraced by the opposite sex

indicators.note: embraced by means the reversed piece sits inside the word for men

parts.note: to a girl, the opposite sex is men

indicators.note: repulsion pushes something back, so the word for turn is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A girl recoils in disgust from the attentions of men.
explanation.walkthrough: Repulsion drives something backwards, which is why 'with repulsion' signals a reversal; from a girl's point of view the opposite sex is men.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a girl's name, used by Shakespeare in Cymbeline.

clue.text: Small space in standard egg

indicators.note: in places the space inside the standard word

parts.note: a grade is a standard or level of quality
an en is a small printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A tiny gap shows up in a grade-one egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is old military slang for a bomb or grenade, not something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Servicemen's slang calls a bomb or hand bomb an egg, so a grenade fits.

clue.text: In a series, preceding first prize Rotherham holds

indicators.note: holds means the answer is held within the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Rotherham football club keeps hold of a trophy won early in a series of games.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeroth describes the position numbered zero, which comes before the first in a sequence.

clue.text: Engineers scrap European steamship, showing no respite

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a morsel is a scrap of food

explanation.surface: Engineers relentlessly break up an old European steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorseless means unrelenting, carrying on without pause or pity.

clue.text: Worried about Greek character

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a Greek person.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a Greek character.

clue.text: Administrator reduced men serving round Royal Academy

indicators.note: round means these pieces go around the academy abbreviation

parts.note: cut means reduced, as in prices cut
RA is the Royal Academy of Arts
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers serving in the army

explanation.surface: An administrator trims the staff working at the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' looks like it trims a word, but it is simply a synonym; 'men serving' is the army's other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator manages a museum or gallery collection, so is a kind of administrator.

clue.text: Become high climbing to achieve peak

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: meat that becomes high starts to rot

explanation.surface: A mountaineer gets light-headed climbing towards a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' suggests altitude; here it is gamey meat going off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, especially on Dartmoor, so it is a peak.

clue.text: Japanese art of note shown by old Baltic city

indicators.note: shown by places the note beside the city

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia, on the Baltic
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A notable Japanese artwork is displayed by an ancient Baltic city.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Old king could become glad thereafter

indicators.note: could become means these letters might be turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch might be cheered by what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century King of Wessex who fought the Vikings.
